$comment: Machine-readable fork layer for this marketplace. The prose version, with the
licence snapshots and the reasoning, stays in the PL hub's THIRD_PARTY_INSPIRATIONS.md
- this file is the part scripts/upstream-delta.py can measure.
relation uses the SAME vocabulary as attribution.relationship in SKILL.md (WM canon
2026-08-05): vendored | adaptation | pattern-only | clean-room | dependency | original.
Deliberately not a second private vocabulary - the gate cross-checks the two, and a
skill claiming LESS provenance than the manifest records is a blocking finding.
map entries are set to what the skill itself declares; mapping an 'original' skill is
legitimate and strict - it polices a no-source claim against the nearest upstream.
pin is written only by `python scripts/upstream-delta.py sync`, and only after the
checkout is verified complete - never by hand.
Snapshots are shared with the PL hub: same pins, one clone, so the twins are measured
against the same upstream commit or not at all.

upstreams.note: Same upstream as the PL twin, same language as the upstream - so unlike humanizer-pl, the text number here is meaningful. This is the skill whose missing MIT notice was the 2026-08-04 defect; attribution-gate polices the claim, this polices the bytes.

upstreams.license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 on the curation; per-skill licence declared in each upstream SKILL.md frontmatter
upstreams.note: The English side of the same adoptions the PL hub declares. These two forks are English-to-English, so a rising text number here is a real signal rather than a translation artefact. The EU AI Act suite is eleven upstream skills policed against the closest one - a known gap, not a clean result.

Verification skills take architecture patterns from lavern. Upstream is TypeScript, ours is markdown: no comparable text surface, so this claim cannot be machine-checked here. Left visible on purpose rather than dropped.
